To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rumen pH and rumen temperature can be monitored by using wireless rumen sensors and that the rumen environment varies depending on the diet and ambient temperature.

rumen temperature and pH can be measured using wireless bolus sensors and that these parameters can be used to evaluate the effects of diet composition, ambient temperature, and feed and water intake.

rumen sensors are useful tools for monitoring the rumen environment in goats and that rumen pH and rumen and rectal temperatures can be used as indicators for assessing the effects of different feeding and climatological conditions on goats' ruminal environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of diet composition and environmental temperature on the rumen environment in dairy goats, using a novel technology to monitor rumen environment in real time.
the development and use of wireless rumen boluses for monitoring pH and temperature in dairy goats and the effects of diet composition and ambient temperature on the rumen environment.
the development of a wireless bolus sensor for monitoring pH and temperature in ruminants and the evaluation of its use to study rumen environment variations in goats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rumen environment is a dynamic system that is highly sensitive to changes in diet and ambient temperature.
the rumen pH was affected by both diet and temperature, whereas the rumen temperature was mainly affected by feeding and ambient temperature.

rumen temperature was more sensitive to the changes in diet composition and ambient temperature, and that rumen pH is less affected by diet composition and more sensitive to the ambient temperature changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rumen pH is more affected than rumen temperature by feeding and climatic changes.
the rumen environment is affected by the diet and the climatic condition, which might affect microbial activity and fermentation.
rumen temperature and pH can be considered as a reliable indicator of the rumen fermentation and the metabolic status of dairy goats, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of rumen sensors is a promising tool to assess rumen pH and to monitor ruminal temperature in nonlateral goats.
